#  Marriage and Divorce in Continuous Time 

## Abstract

This paper reformulates the @greenwood2009 marriage and divorce model in continuous time using the HACT methods of @achdou2022. Replacing the AR(1) match quality process with an Ornstein-Uhlenbeck process yields a tridiagonal generator, reducing the computational complexity of both the value function and stationary distribution calculations from quadratic to linear in the number of grid points. The continuous-time model closely replicates the discrete-time equilibrium across all key outcomes, including the share of married households, the marriage rate, and the divorce rate, while achieving substantial gains in computation time and memory usage.
